newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai banks avg 8 pct non-performing loans - paper.
newsitem.headline: Thai banks avg 8 pct non-performing loans - paper.

text.p: About eight percent of total lending by Thai banks is non-performing loans, a local newspaper reported on Thursday.
Business Day newspaper said the number was an average of total non-performing loans of 13 domestic banks. The figures range from four percent at Bangkok Bank Plc to 10.5 percent at Krung Thai Bank.
The newspaper said the average eight percent figure does not include loans from the Union Bank of Bangkok or the Bangkok Bank of Commerce.
Banks are due to report their non-performing loans to the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) on Thursday.
This is the first time the banks are required to detail their non-performing loans to the public. Previously they released their figures to the SET which then published an average of the sector.
The new rule came out of a shakeup in the finance sector which required banks and finance firms to reveal their non-performing loans in their half-year financial statements.
Thailand is facing its worst economic slowdown and investors are concerned about exposure of banks and finance companies to the cash-strapped property sector.
Among other top banks, Thai Farmers Bank reported 7.4 percent of non-performing loans while Siam Commercial Bank and Bank of Ayudhya each reported six percent, Business Day said.
